guides.title: Big Agnes Copper Spur Models Compared — UL1, UL2, UL3, Bikepack & XL
guides.description: Compare eight current Big Agnes Copper Spur models by capacity, representative catalog weight, official reference price and intended use.
guides.eyebrow: Manually reviewed Copper Spur range guide
guides.intro: The current Copper Spur range shares a three-season, freestanding HyperBead platform, but capacity is only the first decision. Standard models minimize carry weight, Bikepack versions add short poles and bike-mounting storage, and XL versions trade a modest weight and price increase for more room.
guides.verdict: For one backpacker, start with the standard UL1; for two people or a solo camper who values room, the standard UL2 is the most balanced choice; for two people who want extra length and headroom, choose the UL2 XL. Move to a Bikepack model only when its 12-inch pole set and bike-mounting dry bag solve a real packing problem. The UL3 and UL3 XL make the most sense for three sleepers or a roomy two-person setup.
takeaways: Capacity first: UL1, UL2 and UL3 are the one-, two- and three-person branches. A couple should compare UL2 with UL2 XL; a roomy pair should also consider UL3.

Standard models: the representative catalog weights rise from about 0.97 kg for UL1 to 1.19 kg for UL2 and 1.59 kg for UL3. These are the lightest choices at each listed capacity in this eight-model set.

Bikepack trade-off: Bikepack versions add about 390 g, 480 g and 370 g over the corresponding standard UL1, UL2 and UL3 records. In return, Big Agnes lists a 12-inch Shortstik pole set, waterproof dry-bag stuff sack and bike-mounting features.
XL trade-off: UL2 XL adds about 90 g and $50 over UL2; UL3 XL adds about 30 g and $50 over UL3. Big Agnes positions XL around extra length, width and head height rather than a different capacity.

Reference prices: the reviewed official prices run from $499.95 for UL1 to $699.95 for UL3 Bikepack and UL3 XL. Price alone should not decide between standard, Bikepack and XL because each solves a different packing or space need.
Shared platform: all eight official listings describe a three-season, fully freestanding Copper Spur design using HyperBead fabric.
guides.limitations: This is a specification-based buying guide, not a hands-on durability or weather test. Weight values are representative normalized catalog values in our official-source dataset; Big Agnes may separately publish packed, trail or component weights, so do not treat these figures as interchangeable. Prices and availability were checked on 2026-08-03 and can change by market or promotion. The guide covers the current standard UL1/UL2/UL3, Bikepack and XL branches; it intentionally excludes older HV records, mtnGLO variants and larger UL4/UL5 models.

guides.title: Big Agnes Tiger Wall UL2 vs Copper Spur UL2
guides.description: Compare Big Agnes Tiger Wall UL2 and Copper Spur UL2 by representative weight, architecture, official positioning and price.
guides.intro: These two-person Big Agnes tents trade minimum listed weight against structure and feature level. Tiger Wall targets minimalists; Copper Spur emphasizes a freestanding, roomier platform.
takeaways: Weight: Tiger Wall UL2 is listed around 0.99 kg versus 1.19 kg for Copper Spur UL2.
Architecture: Tiger Wall uses a lightweight single-pole architecture; Copper Spur is described as fully freestanding.
Price: Tiger Wall UL2 currently starts about $100 below Copper Spur UL2.
Shared material: both current listings highlight Big Agnes HyperBead fabric.
Decision: prioritize Tiger Wall for the lower representative weight; prioritize Copper Spur when freestanding structure and interior comfort matter more.

guides.title: NEMO Hornet vs Dragonfly vs Dagger OSMO
guides.description: Compare NEMO Hornet, Dragonfly and Dagger OSMO backpacking tents by official positioning, structure and current reference price.
guides.intro: Hornet, Dragonfly and Dagger represent three different priorities in NEMO's backpacking line: minimum weight, balanced freestanding space, and maximum livability.
takeaways: Hornet: NEMO positions it as the ultralight option, using a minimal pole structure and Flybar for added volume.
Dragonfly: the listing emphasizes a freestanding frame and balance between weight and livability.
Dagger: NEMO describes it as the roomiest, most livable backpacking option of the three.
Price: current ranges overlap by capacity; verify the exact person-count variant before comparing totals.
Data limitation: the current catalog lacks normalized weights for these multi-variant listings, so this page does not invent a single figure.

guides.title: Therm-a-Rest NeoAir XLite vs XTherm NXT
guides.description: Compare Therm-a-Rest NeoAir XLite NXT and XTherm NXT sleeping pads by representative weight, official positioning and reference price.
guides.intro: XLite NXT is the lighter all-season model, while XTherm NXT is positioned around maximum warmth-to-weight performance for colder use.
takeaways: Weight: representative catalog weights are about 0.33 kg for XLite NXT and 0.44 kg for XTherm NXT.
Positioning: Therm-a-Rest calls XLite an all-season do-it-all pad and XTherm its warmth-to-weight specialist.
Price: XTherm NXT currently starts about $50 above XLite NXT.
Shape: compare these standard models separately from the wider rectangular MAX variants.
Decision: choose by expected overnight temperatures first, then compare the 110 g representative weight difference.
